Information received since December points to a solid expansion and a strong labor market, while inflation remains below 2 percent but is expected to firm. In line with New Keynesian insights that emphasize the role of expected inflation and real activity (Galí and Gertler, 1999; Woodford, 2003), the Committee’s focus on a symmetric 2 percent goal and gradualism is appropriate: anchored expectations and low market-based inflation compensation argue against an aggressive hiking pace even with unemployment low, consistent with Friedman–Phelps critiques of a long-run inflation–unemployment trade-off. Empirical work on monetary transmission (B. Friedman; Christiano, Eichenbaum, and Evans, 2005) supports the view that an accommodative stance can still bolster real activity in the short run, while Taylor-style policy rules (McCallum and Nelson, 1999; Taylor, 1983) justify signaling further gradual increases as growth and investment are solid. Overall tone: moderately positive on growth with cautious confidence on inflation convergence.
